---
engine: markdown
title: "Carry a table across pages"
subtitle: "Column labels and the current group both reprinted overleaf."
description: "A Keisen table breaks by default, reprinting its column labels and its row-group label on each new page. The show rule a figure needs to do the same."
---

A table breaks by default, so this needs nothing said.
The page height is the only thing the listing sets that the others do not: a page that grows to hold the table never breaks, and breaking is the point here.

```{typst}
//| file: ../../tests/visual/breakable.typ
//| echo: true
//| pages: all
//| layout-ncol: 3
//| alt: "Three pages of one long table. Page one: the title, column labels, and the first rows of the North group. Page two: the column labels and the North group label both reprinted, the group's mean, then the South group. Page three: the last readings, the South group's mean, and the source note."
```

The second page is the point.
Row groups are rendered as native level-3 subheaders, so a group carrying on past a page break reprints its own label under the repeated column labels, and the next group retires it automatically.

## Inside a figure

A table inside a `#figure` does not break, whatever the table was told, until this is in force:

```typst
#show figure: set block(breakable: true)
```

That is the first thing a long table runs into, and nothing about the wrapping says so.
The reference says more about it under [Figures and Quarto](../reference/figures.qmd).
